newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: South African rand and debt markets were stronger late Monday but after last week's volatility they appeared to hold little conviction about where to go next.
"People have been left clueless as to the direction of the market and they are quite keen just to sit back a little bit and just wait," said one bond trader.

Despite some early pondering of the outcome of Tuesday's FOMC meeting, by the afternoon analysts and dealers were predicting muted short-term impact at the most from a move in U.S. rates, for which market expectations remain mixed.

"I really can't see the market putting very much weight on this because whatever happens, fundamentally nothing will have changed. The (South African) central bank's still going to be there on the topside and, rumour has it, on the bottom side," said one rand trader.
At 1405 GMT, the rand was quoted at 4.4680/4710 from Friday's late level of 4.4745/4775.
The unit traded most of the afternoon in a 4.4710-4.5680 channel on meagre turnover after hitting its best level of 4.4665 on late morning exporter interest.

"There's nothing to give the local currency or bond markets new direction. Although, as a general view on both the currency and our bond market I don't think it's being driven by international factors at all," said Deutsche Morgan Grenfell economist Gordon Smith.
In cross rate action, the rand had mixed fortunes and was last at 0.3815/3818 marks from 0.3782/3786 Friday and 7.3199/3293 rand to the British pound from 7.3231/3325 last week.
The unit remained weaker against the yen at 25.9852/0251 from 26.8745/9030 before.

On the bond market, the benchmark R150 security opened strongly on a barrage of jobber-inspired short-covering before settling into a wafer-thin range and prevented to a move better than 14.82 by scattered profit-taking.
The long bond was last at 14.835 from its late Friday level of 14.89.

"We broke through technical levels this morning and we hit another level t 14.82. There doesn't seem to be any serious buying. There a bit of profit-taking from the guys who bought the market down," commented one dealer.
He added the local debt market would likely brush off the FOMC meeting outcome as South Africa was in a different part of the interest rate cycle to the U.S.
South Africa's money market shortage edged back up to 7.974 billion rand on Saturday from 8.050 billion on Friday and 7.780 billion rand on Thursday, the Reserve Bank said.
Domestic money market rates were were unchanged from Friday with three month NCD rates from major banks at 16.40 percent offered and 90-day BA rates at 15.90 percent.
Nominal Bond Exchange turnover slipped to 5.27 billion rand on Friday from 7.48 billion rand on Thursday, a settlement date.
Foreigners were net buyers of 88.09 million rand's worth of South African bonds on Friday after buying 400.98 million rand's worth on Thursday, the Bond Exchange said.
